title: How Billy Dee Williams Finally Became Two-Face After Burton's Batman
excerpt:
Harvey Dent's path to Two-Face was planned after Batman in 1989 but never filmed.
Billy Dee Williams later voiced the villain while Batman '89 comics revisited the idea.
body_md:
Tim Burton's Batman from 1989 is remembered for Michael Keaton's Bruce Wayne and Jack Nicholson's Joker, but another casting decision carried intriguing unrealized possibilities. Billy Dee Williams played Gotham district attorney Harvey Dent, a character who was intended to develop into the villain Two-Face in a later installment. That transformation never appeared in Burton's live-action films.

Williams was already widely recognized as Lando Calrissian from Star Wars. Burton saw cinematic potential in his portrayal of Dent and the visual duality of the character after his transformation. Original Batman screenwriter Sam Hamm included a larger role for Dent in an early treatment for Batman Returns, but Warner Bros. favored the Penguin as a more recognizable principal antagonist.

During development, Daniel Waters replaced Hamm as screenwriter and introduced industrialist Max Shreck, played by Christopher Walken, in place of the planned Dent material. Burton subsequently departed the franchise, and Joel Schumacher's Batman Forever cast Tommy Lee Jones as Two-Face. Williams' interpretation of Dent therefore never underwent the villainous transformation in a live-action sequel.

The actor did eventually return to the character through animation. In The Lego Batman Movie, released in 2017, Williams voiced Two-Face, creating a connection to the role he had played 28 years earlier. He had also voiced Lando in The Lego Movie. His participation was distinctive because he was an original actor reprising a role rather than a performer merely imitating an earlier screen portrayal.

Comic books offered another route for the abandoned storyline. Artist Joe Quinones proposed a continuation of Burton's Batman universe in 2016, but the initial pitch was rejected. DC later published Batman '89 in 2021, written by original screenwriter Sam Hamm and illustrated by Quinones. The six-issue series takes place after Batman Returns and gives Dent a different origin as Two-Face.

In that comic continuity, leaking sulfuric acid from car batteries causes the damage to Dent's face. His behavior deteriorates and he begins relying on a coin to make decisions. The story follows a much darker trajectory than his brief appearance in the original film, with major consequences for Gotham's familiar characters. These events belong to the Batman '89 comic continuity and should not be confused with an announced live-action adaptation.

The verified milestones are Williams' voice performance in 2017 and the comic-book exploration of the character beginning in 2021. Speculation that another Batman film might follow a similar path remains just that: speculation.
